title: Culturing Mammalian Cells in Three-dimensional Peptide Scaffolds
protocol: Prepare a 0.5% solution of peptide RAD16-I in 20% (w/v) sucrose in a micro-centrifuge tube.
Sonicate the peptide solution for 20 minutes in an ultrasonic bath at maximum power and room temperature to ensure homogeneous mixing.
Dilute the prepared peptide solution with the necessary volume of 10% (w/v) sucrose to obtain the desired final concentration.
Place the micro-centrifuge tube containing the diluted peptide solution into an ultrasonic bath at room temperature for 20 minutes to ensure homogeneous mixing.
Store the peptide solution at 4 °C if not used immediately.
Centrifuge the cell suspension obtained after trypsin treatment at 60 x g and room temperature for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant using a Pasteur pipette connected to a vacuum line.
Suspend the cell pellet in 3–5 mL of 10% (w/v) sucrose using a micropipette.
Count cells using a manual or automatic cell counter.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 60 x g and RT for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Suspend the cell pellet again in the necessary volume of 10% (w/v) sucrose to obtain double the desired final cell concentration.
Sonicate the peptide solution prepared in step 1 at maximum power and RT for 5 min.
Pipette and place 40 µL of the cell suspension into a standard micro-centrifuge tube.
Mix an equal volume of the RAD16-I solution in 10% sucrose (w/v) with an equal volume of the cell suspension prepared in step 2 to obtain a suspension of cells in the desired peptide concentration.
Mix by pipetting slowly up and down approximately 10 times.
Using a micropipette, carefully load 80 µL of the suspension into each insert.
Add 0.5 mL of culture media to the bottom of the well to wet the insert membrane.
Let the peptide gel for approximately 20 min in the flow cabinet.
Very slowly add 40 µL of medium to the insert and let it slide down the inner wall to the gel.
Place the plate in the incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere) for 20 min.
Add 60 µL of medium to the inner wall of the insert, allowing it to flow down the wall.
Aspirate the medium of the well, which is rich in sucrose, and add 0.5 mL of fresh medium.
Add 60 µL of medium slowly to the insert and place the plate in the incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere) for 10 min.
Aspirate the medium of the well and add 2.5 mL of fresh medium into the well.
Add 200 µL of medium into the insert.
Place the plate in the incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere).
Change the medium every day.
Remove the old medium from the bottom of the well.
Add 2.5 mL of fresh medium to the well and 200 μL to the insert.
Prepare the necessary volume of a fresh solution of 2 µM calcein AM and 2 µM of ethidium homodimer-1 (EthD-1) in PBS by vortexing for 10 s.
Keep the prepared solution in the dark.
Rinse the 3D-SAPS samples 3 times with 2 mL of PBS using a micropipette.
Cover the rinsed samples with the solution prepared in step 4.1.
Incubate it at RT for 40 min in the dark.
Rinse the constructs with 2 mL of PBS 5 times using a micropipette.
Visualize the samples under a fluorescence microscope using 10X or 20X magnification.
Culture cells (37 °C, 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere) in Chondrocyte Basal Medium (CBM) with growth supplements.

Induce cell differentiation at day 2 with chondrogenic medium containing recombinant human transforming growth factor-b1 [TGFb1] (10 ng/mL), L-Ascorbic Acid 2-phosphate [AA2P] (25 µg/mL) and Dexamethasone (100 nM).
Maintain the culture for 4 weeks in an incubator with a humidified atmosphere at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Change chondrogenic medium every other day.
Wash 3D-SAPS cultures twice by adding and then removing 2 mL of PBS using a micropipette.
Fix the samples by adding 2 mL of 2% (w/v) p-formaldehyde in PBS for 2 h at room temperature.
Wash the fixed samples twice with 2 mL of 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS.
Incubate the samples with 2 mL of 0.05% Toluidine Blue in water for 20 min at room temperature.
Wash the samples several times (at least three times) with 2 mL of PBS until the solution is clear.
Analyze the samples by visual inspection under a stereoscopic microscope.
Lyse 3D-constructs in RIPA buffer containing protease inhibitor cocktail by pipetting.
Prepare an acrylamide gel according to specific volume requirements and run cell lysates for 90 min at 150 V.
Prepare acrylamide gel at a concentration of 7.5–10% (w/v).
Transfer proteins from the gel into a PVDF membrane by applying 40 V for 2 h at room temperature.
Incubate the PVDF membrane at room temperature for 2 h in blocking buffer (4% (w/v) nonfat powdered milk in PBST).
Incubate the membrane at room temperature for 1 h with primary antibodies at a final concentration of 1 mg/mL in PBST.
Add secondary antibodies at a concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Prepare the membrane for detection with a chemiluminescent substrate.
Take chemiluminescent images.
